The pipeline still includes baseline generation, activation extraction, steering vector computation, and steering evaluation, but with an increased task count for better statistical resolution and explicit logging of extraction pool sizes, per-coefficient behaviour counts, accuracies, and success rates. import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import os, re

working_dir = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "working")
os.makedirs(working_dir, exist_ok=True)

try:
    experiment_data = np.load(
        os.path.join(working_dir, "experiment_data.npy"), allow_pickle=True
    ).item()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error loading experiment data: {e}")
    experiment_data = {}

root = experiment_data.get("steering_analysis", {}).get("r1_distill_llama_8b", {})
dose_response = root.get("dose_response", {})
bse_scores = root.get("bse_scores", {})
layer_ablation = root.get("layer_ablation", {})
interference = root.get("cross_interference", {})
baseline = root.get("baseline", {})
preds = root.get("predictions", [])
gts = root.get("ground_truth", [])
baseline_acc = baseline.get("accuracy", None)

# Plot 1: Dose-response behaviour count curves
try:
    plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
    for b, r in dose_response.items():
        cs = sorted([float(k) for k in r.keys()])
        ys = [r[str(c)]["target_mean"] for c in cs]
        plt.plot(cs, ys, "o-", label=b)
    plt.xlabel("Steering coefficient (× BASE_SCALE)")
    plt.ylabel("Mean target behaviour count in CoT")
    plt.title(
        "R1-Distill-Llama-8B (Math): Dose-Response Curves\nBehaviour frequency vs steering coefficient (mid layer)"
    )
    plt.legend()
    plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(os.path.join(working_dir, "r1_llama8b_dose_response_curves.png"))
    plt.close()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error creating dose-response plot: {e}")
    plt.close()

# Plot 2: Accuracy vs coefficient
try:
    plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
    for b, r in dose_response.items():
        cs = sorted([float(k) for k in r.keys()])
        ys = [r[str(c)]["acc"] for c in cs]
        plt.plot(cs, ys, "s-", label=b)
    if baseline_acc is not None:
        plt.axhline(
            baseline_acc, color="k", ls="--", label=f"baseline={baseline_acc:.2f}"
        )
    plt.xlabel("Steering coefficient")
    plt.ylabel("Task accuracy")
    plt.ylim(0, 1.05)
    plt.title(
        "R1-Distill-Llama-8B (Math): Task Accuracy vs Steering Coefficient\nPer behaviour steering vector"
    )
    plt.legend()
    plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(os.path.join(working_dir, "r1_llama8b_accuracy_vs_coefficient.png"))
    plt.close()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error creating accuracy plot: {e}")
    plt.close()

# Plot 3: BSE scores bar chart
try:
    if bse_scores:
        plt.figure(figsize=(7, 4))
        bs = list(bse_scores.keys())
        ys_a1 = [bse_scores[b]["bse_a1"] for b in bs]
        ys_a2 = [
            bse_scores[b]["bse_a2"] if bse_scores[b].get("bse_a2") is not None else 0.0
            for b in bs
        ]
        x = np.arange(len(bs))
        w = 0.35
        plt.bar(x - w / 2, ys_a1, w, label="BSE (α=1)", color="steelblue")
        plt.bar(x + w / 2, ys_a2, w, label="BSE (α=2)", color="orange")
        plt.xticks(x, bs, rotation=20)
        plt.ylabel("BSE score")
        plt.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.5)
        plt.title(
            "R1-Distill-Llama-8B (Math): Behaviour Steering Efficacy\nComparison of α=1 vs α=2 coefficients"
        )
        plt.legend()
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(os.path.join(working_dir, "r1_llama8b_bse_scores.png"))
        plt.close()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error creating BSE plot: {e}")
    plt.close()

# Plot 4: Per-layer ablation for hedging
try:
    hedge_abl = layer_ablation.get("hedging", {})
    if hedge_abl:
        lis = sorted([int(k) for k in hedge_abl.keys()])
        deltas = [hedge_abl[str(li)]["delta"] for li in lis]
        bses = [hedge_abl[str(li)]["bse"] for li in lis]
        accs_pos = [hedge_abl[str(li)]["acc_pos"] for li in lis]
        accs_neg = [hedge_abl[str(li)]["acc_neg"] for li in lis]
        fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
        ax1.plot(
            lis, deltas, "o-", color="steelblue", label="Δ freq (+coeff vs -coeff)"
        )
        ax1.plot(lis, bses, "s-", color="green", label="BSE")
        ax1.set_xlabel("Transformer layer index")
        ax1.set_ylabel("Δ / BSE")
        ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        ax2 = ax1.twinx()
        ax2.plot(lis, accs_pos, "^--", color="red", alpha=0.6, label="acc (+coeff)")
        ax2.plot(lis, accs_neg, "v--", color="purple", alpha=0.6, label="acc (-coeff)")
        ax2.set_ylabel("Accuracy")
        ax2.set_ylim(0, 1.05)
        lines1, labels1 = ax1.get_legend_handles_labels()
        lines2, labels2 = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
        ax1.legend(lines1 + lines2, labels1 + labels2, loc="best", fontsize=8)
        plt.title(
            "R1-Distill-Llama-8B (Math): Per-Layer Steering Ablation for 'hedging'\nLeft axis: Δ/BSE, Right axis: accuracy"
        )
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(os.path.join(working_dir, "r1_llama8b_layer_ablation_hedging.png"))
        plt.close()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error creating layer ablation plot: {e}")
    plt.close()

# Plot 5: Cross-behaviour interference heatmap
try:
    if interference:
        src = list(interference.keys())
        tgt = sorted({t for r in interference.values() for t in r.keys()})
        M = np.array([[interference[s].get(t, 0.0) for t in tgt] for s in src])
        vmax = max(np.abs(M).max(), 1e-6)
        plt.figure(figsize=(6.5, 5.5))
        im = plt.imshow(M, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-vmax, vmax=vmax)
        plt.xticks(range(len(tgt)), tgt, rotation=30)
        plt.yticks(range(len(src)), src)
        plt.xlabel("Target behaviour (measured)")
        plt.ylabel("Source behaviour (steered)")
        plt.title(
            "R1-Distill-Llama-8B (Math): Cross-Behaviour Interference\nΔ = f(coeff=+1) - f(coeff=-1)"
        )
        for i in range(len(src)):
            for j in range(len(tgt)):
                plt.text(j, i, f"{M[i,j]:.1f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8)
        plt.colorbar(im)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(
            os.path.join(working_dir, "r1_llama8b_cross_interference_heatmap.png")
        )
        plt.close()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error creating interference heatmap: {e}")
    plt.close()

# Plot 6: Baseline behaviour totals
try:
    bc = baseline.get("counts", {})
    if bc:
        plt.figure(figsize=(7, 4))
        behs = list(bc.keys())
        vals = [bc[b] for b in behs]
        plt.bar(behs, vals, color="teal")
        plt.ylabel("Total occurrences across baseline CoTs")
        plt.title(
            "R1-Distill-Llama-8B (Math): Baseline Behaviour Totals\nUnsteered chain-of-thought"
        )
        plt.xticks(rotation=20)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(
            os.path.join(working_dir, "r1_llama8b_baseline_behaviour_totals.png")
        )
        plt.close()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error creating baseline totals plot: {e}")
    plt.close()

# Plot 7: Per-task correctness for baseline
try:
    if preds and gts:

        def parse_num(p):
            try:
                s = re.sub(r"[^0-9\.\-]", "", str(p))
                return float(s) if s not in ("", "-", ".", "-.") else None
            except:
                return None

        flags = []
        for p, g in zip(preds, gts):
            v = parse_num(p)
            flags.append(1 if (v is not None and abs(v - float(g)) < 1e-3) else 0)
        plt.figure(figsize=(10, 3))
        idx = np.arange(len(flags))
        colors = ["green" if c == 1 else "red" for c in flags]
        plt.bar(idx, flags, color=colors)
        plt.xlabel("Task index")
        plt.ylabel("Correct (1) / Incorrect (0)")
        acc_str = f"{baseline_acc:.3f}" if baseline_acc is not None else "N/A"
        plt.title(
            f"R1-Distill-Llama-8B (Math): Baseline Per-Task Correctness (acc={acc_str})\nGreen=correct, Red=incorrect"
        )
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(os.path.join(working_dir, "r1_llama8b_baseline_correctness.png"))
        plt.close()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error creating correctness plot: {e}")
    plt.close()

# Plot 8: Comparison - target vs off-target behaviour change under steering
try:
    if dose_response:
        behs = list(dose_response.keys())
        target_deltas = []
        offtarget_deltas = []
        for b in behs:
            r = dose_response[b]
            if "1.0" in r and "-1.0" in r:
                pos_means = r["1.0"]["all_means"]
                neg_means = r["-1.0"]["all_means"]
                target_deltas.append(pos_means[b] - neg_means[b])
                off = [pos_means[k] - neg_means[k] for k in pos_means if k != b]
                offtarget_deltas.append(np.mean(off) if off else 0.0)
        x = np.arange(len(behs))
        w = 0.35
        plt.figure(figsize=(7, 4))
        plt.bar(
            x - w / 2, target_deltas, w, label="Target behaviour Δ", color="steelblue"
        )
        plt.bar(
            x + w / 2, offtarget_deltas, w, label="Mean off-target Δ", color="salmon"
        )
        plt.xticks(x, behs, rotation=20)
        plt.ylabel("Δ frequency (coeff=+1 vs -1)")
        plt.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.5)
        plt.title(
            "R1-Distill-Llama-8B (Math): Target vs Off-Target Steering Effect\nHigher target Δ + lower off-target Δ = more selective steering"
        )
        plt.legend()
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(os.path.join(working_dir, "r1_llama8b_target_vs_offtarget.png"))
        plt.close()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error creating target vs off-target plot: {e}")
    plt.close()

# Print metrics
try:
    print(f"Baseline accuracy: {baseline_acc}")
    print(f"Baseline behaviour counts: {baseline.get('counts', {})}")
    for b, s in bse_scores.items():
        print(f"BSE[{b}]: α=1 -> {s['bse_a1']:.3f}, α=2 -> {s.get('bse_a2')}")
    for b, r in dose_response.items():
        print(f"Dose-response[{b}]:")
        for c in sorted(r.keys(), key=lambda x: float(x)):
            print(
                f"  coeff={c}: target_mean={r[c]['target_mean']:.2f}, acc={r[c]['acc']:.3f}"
            )
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error printing metrics: {e}")

plot_analyses.analysis: Bar chart titled 'Behavior Presence Rates on 500-task Reasoning Benchmark' showing percentage of chains containing each behavior. Only one behavior category ('validation') is visible with ~24% presence rate. The plot appears sparse - either most behaviors were not detected or only one category was successfully analyzed. This is a weak initial characterization since the taxonomy should include uncertainty/hedging, backtracking, self-correction, and example-generation, but most are absent from the visualization.

Line plot titled 'Dose-Response: Steering Coefficient vs Validation Behavior Rate' showing behavior rate (%) vs steering coefficient from -3 to +3. The curve is essentially flat at ~24% across all coefficient values (both positive and negative), with only a tiny bump near coefficient=1. This is a CRITICAL NEGATIVE RESULT: the steering vector shows NO dose-dependent effect on the target behavior. This directly contradicts the core hypothesis that adding/subtracting the steering vector amplifies/suppresses the behavior in a dose-dependent manner.

Line plot titled 'Downstream Accuracy vs Steering Coefficient' showing accuracy percentage vs steering coefficient. The line is roughly flat around 32-36% accuracy with minor fluctuations. Accuracy is preserved across steering strengths, which partially supports the hypothesis that steering preserves task accuracy. However, this is a hollow victory given that the steering also fails to change behavior (plot 2), so preservation of accuracy is trivial when nothing is being steered.

Heatmap titled 'Layer Sweep: Behavior Rate by Layer and Coefficient' showing behavior rates across layers 4-28 and coefficients -2 to +2. Values are nearly uniform around 22-26% across the entire grid, with no clear layer showing strong steering effects. Some slight variation exists (e.g., layer 24 with coefficient +2 shows 26%), but no systematic dose-response pattern emerges at any layer. This suggests the linear steering vector approach is not finding an effective intervention point in the residual stream.

Bar chart titled 'Prompt Engineering vs Steering Vector Comparison'. Shows validation rate for baseline (~24%), prompt-encourage (~30%), and steer+2 (~24%). Prompt engineering shows a modest positive effect (~6 percentage point increase) while steering has essentially no effect. This is a negative finding for the hypothesis - prompt engineering appears MORE effective than steering vectors, contradicting the claim that steering provides finer-grained control.

Line plot titled 'Cross-Model Generalization: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B'. Shows behavior rate flat at ~40% across coefficient range -2 to +2, with baseline being slightly higher than steered variants. Again no dose-response relationship. The steering vector extracted from one model does not transfer to another model in the R1-Distill family, further weakening the generalizability claim.

Line plot titled 'OOD Transfer: MATH/GSM8K/AIME Accuracy vs Coefficient'. Shows three curves (MATH, GSM8K, AIME) all relatively flat with small fluctuations across coefficients -2 to +2. Accuracy is preserved on out-of-distribution benchmarks but no meaningful behavioral change is induced. Consistent with the null finding that the steering vectors don't functionally modulate reasoning behaviors.

Bar chart titled 'Behavior Composition: Steered vs Unsteered Chains' showing composition of different behaviors (validation, backtracking, uncertainty, example-gen) in unsteered vs steered chains. The bars for both conditions look nearly identical across all behavior categories, confirming that steering does not change the composition of reasoning behaviors in generated chains. This is arguably the most damaging result for the hypothesis.

best node.vlm_feedback_summary: The experimental results provide substantial evidence AGAINST the main research hypothesis that reasoning behaviors in thinking LLMs are linearly steerable. Key findings: (1) The dose-response curves are essentially flat, showing no amplification or suppression of behaviors with varying steering coefficients; (2) A layer sweep reveals no effective intervention point in the residual stream; (3) Prompt engineering appears MORE effective than steering vectors, directly contradicting a core claim of the paper; (4) Cross-model generalization fails - steering vectors don't transfer to other R1-Distill models; (5) Behavior composition in steered vs unsteered chains is nearly identical. While downstream accuracy is preserved (partially supporting one sub-claim), this is trivial given nothing is being steered. Additionally, the initial behavior detection appears to have only successfully identified one behavior category ('validation'), suggesting weaknesses in the taxonomy annotation or detection pipeline. The experiments as currently designed do not support publication - the researcher should either (a) investigate why steering is ineffective (e.g., try non-linear probes, difference-of-means with better contrastive pairs, layer-wise interventions with proper hooks, or the ITI/CAA methods with proper normalization), or (b) reframe the paper around the negative finding that these behaviors are NOT linearly steerable, which would itself be an interesting contribution challenging recent activation steering literature.

plot_analyses.analysis: Bar chart showing reasoning behavior distribution counts (approximately 1-2 per category) across 10 categories including uncertainty, backtracking, example generation, etc. Counts are extremely low (mostly 1-2), suggesting the taxonomy annotation was applied to a very small pilot sample. This indicates the pipeline works but statistical power is limited. The categories look reasonable but the frequencies show class imbalance concerns for downstream steering vector extraction.

Line plot showing steering vector norm growth across transformer layers (0-30) for the DeepSeek-R1-Distill model. Uncertainty (blue), backtracking (orange), and example generation (green) directions all show near-linear increase in norm with layer depth, reaching ~30-80 at layer 30. This is consistent with prior findings that intervention magnitudes scale with layer depth, but the near-identical trajectories across behaviors may suggest the vectors are not well-separated or that norms are dominated by general activation growth rather than behavior-specific structure.

Dose-response plot showing behavior frequency vs steering coefficient (-3 to +3) for three behaviors. Curves are largely flat/noisy with minor variations, and behaviors do not show clean monotonic dose-response relationships. This is a critical negative result: the linear steering hypothesis predicts smooth monotonic amplification/suppression, but the observed weak/flat responses suggest either (a) coefficients tested are too small, (b) steering vectors are poorly extracted, or (c) behaviors are not truly linearly encoded. Needs investigation.

Accuracy vs steering coefficient plot showing task accuracy remains roughly stable (around 0.5-0.7) across coefficient range [-3, 3] for all three behaviors. This supports the claim that steering preserves downstream accuracy - a positive result. However, given the weak dose-response in the previous plot, this stability may simply reflect that the steering interventions are having minimal effect overall rather than demonstrating fine-grained control without accuracy cost.

Cosine similarity heatmap between behavior direction vectors. Diagonal shows self-similarity (1.0) and off-diagonal values appear moderate to high (0.3-0.6 range typical for such analyses). High off-diagonal similarity would indicate the behavior directions are not orthogonal/independent, which challenges the hypothesis that each behavior has its own distinct linear direction. This is important diagnostic evidence about whether behaviors are truly separable in activation space.

Comparison plot of steering effects vs prompt engineering baseline. Shows steering (blue) vs prompting (orange) approaches across behaviors. If steering shows finer-grained control (smoother gradients) than prompting's binary on/off effect, it would support the finer-grained control claim. However, results appear mixed - would need clearer separation to demonstrate steering's advantage over prompting.

Cross-model transfer plot showing steering vector effectiveness across model sizes (1.5B, 8B, 14B). Tests whether behavior directions extracted from 8B transfer to other R1-Distill variants. Transfer results would validate the generality of linear behavior representations. The plot suggests some transferability but with degradation, which is expected and interesting for the paper's cross-scale generalization claims.

OOD benchmark evaluation (MATH/GSM8K/AIME) showing steering effects on out-of-distribution reasoning tasks. Tests whether steering vectors extracted on the custom 500-task benchmark generalize to standard reasoning benchmarks. Shows the practical utility of the approach beyond the training distribution, which is important for the paper's broader claims.

Layer-wise steering effect analysis showing which transformer layers are most effective for behavior steering. Different behaviors may have optimal intervention layers (mid-to-late layers typically). This provides mechanistic insight and practical guidance for where to apply steering. The pattern across layers helps validate that the linear representations emerge at specific processing stages.

Ablation or additional analysis plot - likely showing sensitivity of results to contrastive pair selection, number of pairs used for direction extraction, or comparison of extraction methods (mean-difference vs PCA vs probing). Such analyses are important for demonstrating robustness of the extracted steering vectors.

The pipeline consists of baseline generation, activation extraction, steering vector computation, and steering evaluation with several key scientific components: (1) expanding the steering coefficient range to [-2, -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, 2] to characterize full dose-response curves for each behaviour; (2) performing per-layer steering ablations across a subset of transformer layers to identify the optimal intervention layer per behaviour; (3) computing the formal Behaviour Steering Efficacy (BSE) metric as specified in the requirements; (4) investigating the backtracking sign-flip anomaly by examining the quality and direction of extracted steering vectors; and (5) cross-behaviour interference analysis (e.g., steering hedging while measuring backtracking) to test specificity. An increased task count improves statistical resolution, with explicit logging of extraction pool sizes, per-coefficient behaviour counts, accuracies, and success rates. The current step extends this by aggregating results across multiple random seeds, providing variance estimates and improved statistical reliability across all analyses (dose-response, per-layer ablations, BSE, sign-flip investigation, and cross-behaviour interference).

        beh_union.update(r.get("baseline", {}).get("counts", {}).keys())
    behs = sorted(beh_union)
    if behs:
        stack = []
        for r in roots:
            bc = r.get("baseline", {}).get("counts", {})
            stack.append([bc.get(b, np.nan) for b in behs])
        arr = np.array(stack, dtype=float)
        m = np.nanmean(arr, axis=0)
        c = np.sum(~np.isnan(arr), axis=0)
        s = (
            np.nanstd(arr, axis=0, ddof=1) / np.sqrt(np.maximum(c, 1))
            if arr.shape[0] > 1
            else np.zeros_like(m)
        )
        plt.figure(figsize=(8, 4.5))
        x = np.arange(len(behs))
        plt.bar(x, m, yerr=s, capsize=3, color="teal", label="mean ± SEM")
        plt.xticks(x, behs, rotation=20)
        plt.ylabel("Total occurrences in baseline CoTs")
        plt.title(
            f"R1-Distill-Llama-8B (Math): Aggregated Baseline Behaviour Totals\nMean ± SEM across {n_runs} run(s)"
        )
        plt.legend()
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(
            os.path.join(working_dir, "agg_r1_llama8b_baseline_behaviour_totals.png")
        )
        plt.close()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error creating aggregated baseline totals plot: {e}")
    plt.close()

# Aggregate target vs off-target Δ
try:
    behs = set()
    for r in roots:
        behs.update(r.get("dose_response", {}).keys())
    behs = sorted(behs)
    if behs:
        tgt_stack, off_stack = [], []
        for r in roots:
            row_t, row_o = [], []
            for b in behs:
                dr = r.get("dose_response", {}).get(b, {})
                if "1.0" in dr and "-1.0" in dr:
                    pos_means = dr["1.0"].get("all_means", {})
                    neg_means = dr["-1.0"].get("all_means", {})
                    row_t.append(pos_means.get(b, np.nan) - neg_means.get(b, np.nan))
                    off = [
                        pos_means[k] - neg_means[k]
                        for k in pos_means
                        if k != b and k in neg_means
                    ]
                    row_o.append(np.mean(off) if off else np.nan)
                else:
                    row_t.append(np.nan)
                    row_o.append(np.nan)
            tgt_stack.append(row_t)
            off_stack.append(row_o)
        T = np.array(tgt_stack, dtype=float)
        O = np.array(off_stack, dtype=float)

        def ms(a):
            m = np.nanmean(a, axis=0)
            c = np.sum(~np.isnan(a), axis=0)
            s = (
                np.nanstd(a, axis=0, ddof=1) / np.sqrt(np.maximum(c, 1))
                if a.shape[0] > 1
                else np.zeros_like(m)
            )
            return m, s

        tm, ts = ms(T)
        om, os_ = ms(O)
        x = np.arange(len(behs))
        w = 0.35
        plt.figure(figsize=(8, 4.5))
        plt.bar(
            x - w / 2,
            tm,
            w,
            yerr=ts,
            capsize=3,
            label="Target Δ (mean±SEM)",
            color="steelblue",
        )
        plt.bar(
            x + w / 2,
            om,
            w,
            yerr=os_,
            capsize=3,
            label="Off-target Δ (mean±SEM)",
            color="salmon",
        )
        plt.xticks(x, behs, rotation=20)
        plt.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.5)
        plt.ylabel("Δ frequency (coeff=+1 vs -1)")
        plt.title(
            f"R1-Distill-Llama-8B (Math): Aggregated Target vs Off-Target Steering\nMean ± SEM across {n_runs} run(s)"
        )
        plt.legend()
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(os.path.join(working_dir, "agg_r1_llama8b_target_vs_offtarget.png"))
        plt.close()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error creating aggregated target vs off-target plot: {e}")
    plt.close()

# Print aggregated metrics
try:
    baseline_accs = [r.get("baseline", {}).get("accuracy", None) for r in roots]
    baseline_accs = [x for x in baseline_accs if x is not None]
    if baseline_accs:
        print(
            f"Baseline accuracy: mean={np.mean(baseline_accs):.3f}, "
            f"sem={(np.std(baseline_accs, ddof=1)/np.sqrt(len(baseline_accs))) if len(baseline_accs)>1 else 0.0:.3f}, "
            f"n={len(baseline_accs)}"
        )
    behs = set()
    for r in roots:
        behs.update(r.get("bse_scores", {}).keys())
    for b in sorted(behs):
        a1 = [r.get("bse_scores", {}).get(b, {}).get("bse_a1", np.nan) for r in roots]
        a1 = [x for x in a1 if not (x is None or np.isnan(x))]
        if a1:
            m = np.mean(a1)
            s = (np.std(a1, ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(a1))) if len(a1) > 1 else 0.0
            print(f"BSE[{b}] α=1: mean={m:.3f} ± {s:.3f} (n={len(a1)})")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error printing aggregated metrics: {e}")
